chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid said, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Rabi', on the authority of Fudayl ibn Yasar, that I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.' He (AS) replied, 'O Fudayl! The heavens and the earth and everything in the Kursi.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the 'Kursi' (Throne/Seat) encompasses not only the heavens and earth but all created entities, emphasizing the totality of divine containment. This interpretation aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition distinguishing the Kursi as a vast realm of knowledge and power, distinct yet related to the Arsh (Throne), thereby illustrating the infinite scope of Allah's dominion.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan alSaffar said: Ya`qub ibn Yazid said, on the authority of Hammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of Rabi`I, on the authority of Fjudayl ibn Yasar that I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS)

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: His knowledge extends over the heaves and the earth.’ Consequently, he (AS) replied, “O Fudayl! The heavens and the earth and everything between them, are in the Throne.”
